name: Termination Barriers for Mutually Recursive Duplicating Cycles
description: Shows finite cyclic delayed-duplication systems admit no additive or unbounded-affine orientation. Every bounded cycle realizes its path with executable search sound and complete.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: Every finite cyclic delayed-duplication system realizes its one-cycle path by transitive closure yet admits no additive and, when the derived one-cycle witness is unbounded, no affine global orientation, with executable cycle search sound and complete.
summary: The theory studies finite cyclic mutually recursive systems where each successor step peels a successor and wraps the next recursor, with delayed duplication appearing after one full cycle. It asks which measure families can orient the minimal contextual closure decreasingly and whether the cycle path is realized and found by search. It defines first-class k+1-node schemas and systems, cycle sources and targets, additive and affine measures, builders, graph-search certificates, encoded search spaces and final catalogs. It shows every such system realizes its source-to-target path in the transitive closure of the contextual relation, and that no additive measure globally orients it. Under unboundedness of the derived one-cycle affine witness, no affine measure globally orients it either. It packages these facts into theorem-visible final and algorithmic catalogs, with executable search that is sound when it returns a candidate, complete when all successor edges are present, and reports a typed missing-edge status otherwise, witnessed by concrete two- and three-rule systems.
boundary: On the realization side every bounded finite cycle with certified successor steps reaches its wrapped target by transitive closure of the contextual relation, while on the orientation side no additive measure and no unbounded affine measure can decrease along all those steps. The obstruction is the realized one-cycle composite itself, which forces any candidate measure to rise from source to target: additive pumps always rise, affine pumps rise when the derived one-cycle witness is unbounded, and wrapper dominance or transparency marks the same limit in preserving variants. The finite-cycle no-go theorems, their final-catalog projections and the packet-cycle non-well-foundedness locate this boundary, while executable search succeeds on the realizable side and reports a missing edge on the failure side.

conclusions.statement: For every finite-cycle system, builder, search certificate or graph-search certificate and every additive measure M, M with Nat less-than does not globally orient the contextual relation; a final catalog hypothesis projects the same barrier for its certificate.

For every finite-cycle system and every affine measure M and node i, if the derived one-cycle witness at i, in particular at node 0, has unbounded range then M with Nat less-than does not globally orient the contextual relation.

For every finite-cycle system, builder or certificate, every index i and all terms b s n, the cycle source reaches the cycle target by TransGen of the contextual relation; a final catalog projects the same TransGen realization at any index.
Every graph-search certificate C satisfies the finite-cycle mutual-duplication final catalog.
Every encoded search space S satisfies the algorithmic-search final catalog with soundness, finite completeness and missing-edge boundary.

If executable search over an encoded space returns some candidate W, then W yields a graph-search certificate and its final catalog; with an algorithmic catalog hypothesis the same success projects the finite-cycle catalog.
If every required successor edge is present in an encoded search space, then executable search returns some witness candidate, and an algorithmic catalog hypothesis projects the same completeness.
For every encoded search space S, searchCycle? S returns none if and only if the missing-successor-edge status for S is nonempty.

For all b s n, the concrete two-rule and three-rule witness systems realize their finite-cycle path by TransGen, satisfy the final catalog, and their encoded spaces have succeeding executable searches.
For every finite SCC certificate C, TransGen of the induced rewrite step holds in both directions between the two witness packets, and the reverse TransGen relation on packets is not well-founded.
For every finite SCC certificate C, there is no interpretation of nodes into Trace sending every edge to a Step.

For the finite preserving cyclic system no additive eval globally orients StepCtx, while the explicit affine escape measure makes every synchronized target eval below its source, so it is false that every affine measure fails to orient the cycle, and the boundary record pairing these facts is inhabited, recording both sides.

Given a compositional measure with successor transparent at base with c_succ c_base = c_base, its eval does not globally orient the finite-cycle or two-rule mutual context; given a scalar projection strictly increasing with R and matching an unbounded affine eval, no R-orientation of that context exists.

If a nontrivial SCC pair is found, or a two-sided TransGen round-trip holds, then for every additive measure M, M with Nat less-than does not globally orient the delayed or preserving contextual relation.

openPoints: Affine barriers require unbounded range of the derived one-cycle witness, with separate node-i and node-0 variants.
Compositional barriers require successor transparency at base with c_succ c_base = c_base.
Scalar-projection barriers require strict projection of the target order to Nat plus agreement with an unbounded affine eval or a transparent eval.
Preserving affine barriers require wrapper dominance plus unbounded eval; without dominance an explicit escape measure orients the cycle, so the unrestricted affine claim fails.

Relational, call-graph and extracted barriers require a certified cycle, two-sided round-trip, nontrivial SCC or found SCC pair; without such a witness no barrier is claimed and results do not extend to unbounded arbitrary graphs.

Certificates store successor-step or edge data explicitly and do not discover edges algorithmically; raw extraction needs a separate bridge, and supplied successor edges plus step witnesses suffice without a necessity claim.

Executable search checks the predetermined successor edges of the supplied encoded cycle; success needs all edges present and failure yields a typed missing-edge status, not arbitrary graph discovery.

The closeout covers the listed ten-row finite surface with nine theorem-covered rows and one typed-boundary missing-edge row; coexistence results assert joint holding without any map from graph nodes or edges to Trace terms or rewrite steps.

files.summary: This file supplies the missing transport from finite SCC certificates to a rewrite relation on packet syntax. It defines single-node packets with edges as rewrite steps and lifts graph reachability and the SCC round-trip to a cycle between distinct packets. It proves the induced reverse relation is never well-founded, while no edge-respecting interpretation into terminating Trace steps exists.
files.conclusion: Every finite SCC certificate yields a nonterminating packet rewrite cycle, but no edge-respecting map into terminating KO7 Step exists.

files.summary: This file packages a finite decidable graph with a nontrivial SCC beside independent KO7 boundary results. It defines the FiniteSCCCertificate structure and the canonical two-node Bool certificate with its nontrivial SCC. It proves every certificate yields an abstract round-trip and bundles it with the contextual-to-root orientation projection and the direct-observer barrier as coexistence without edge-to-rewrite transport.
files.conclusion: Every finite SCC certificate contributes an abstract round-trip that coexists with, but does not map into, the KO7 orientation and direct-observer impossibilities.

files.summary: This file builds delayed and preserving SCC barrier systems from finite extracted call graphs. From node keys and successor-key sets it constructs the relation-level systems automatically. It reexports additive, affine, transparent and scalar-projection barriers guarded by a found nontrivial SCC pair.
files.conclusion: Call-graph presentations with a found nontrivial SCC inherit the relational additive, affine and transparent barriers.

files.summary: This file implements an alternating two-function duplicating example where each root rule copies the step argument. One root step plus one step under wrap yields three occurrences of the step argument. Uniform additive measures with positive wrapper weight are pumped by wrapper chains and cannot orient the displayed two-step composite.
files.conclusion: No uniform additive measure orients the alternating two-step duplicating composite.

files.summary: This file isolates the delayed-duplication cycle from iterated successors to nested wrappers. It transports affine and compositional measures to the derived one-cycle schema. It rederives additive, affine, transparent-compositional and scalar-projection contextual barriers from that single witness.
files.conclusion: Any contextual relation realizing the delayed cycle is blocked for additive, affine, transparent and projected measures.

files.summary: This file builds delayed and preserving call-graph presentations from array-backed extracted node data with local step theorems. It defines conversions to the existing call-graph systems and measure and orientation aliases. It proves that a found nontrivial SCC pair blocks additive, affine, compositional-transparent and scalar-projection global orientations under the usual unboundedness, dominance or transparency hypotheses.
files.conclusion: Both delayed and preserving extracted-data presentations inherit additive, affine, compositional-transparent and scalar-projection contextual no-orientation barriers from the call-graph stack whenever a nontrivial SCC pair is found.

files.summary: This file introduces first-class finite nonempty mutual-recursion schemas and systems factored through the k+1-node interface, with cycle source and target operations. It proves additive impossibility for direct orienters and affine impossibility under an unbounded one-cycle pump, plus contextual versions via realized TransGen paths. It bridges the native two-rule schema and system to length-2 cycles and supplies concrete two-rule and three-rule witness systems with realized paths.
files.conclusion: Every bounded finite-cycle system realizes its one-cycle path and admits no additive and, under unboundedness, no affine global orientation, with concrete two-rule and three-rule witnesses.

files.summary: This module exposes the validated H3 final catalog through stable API aliases for certificates, encoded spaces, candidates and failure statuses. It projects cycle realization and additive and affine barriers, soundness, completeness and missing-edge boundaries for successful searches. It adds no new theorem program and records that certified successor edges suffice while raw algorithmic extraction needs a separate bridge.
files.conclusion: The validated H3 final catalog, its cycle realization and additive and affine barriers, plus executable soundness, completeness and two- and three-rule witnesses, are exposed under stable API names.

files.summary: This file defines explicit finite encoded search spaces with edge lookups and the searchCycle? procedure that checks predetermined successor edges. It proves soundness to graph-search certificates, completeness when all successor edges exist, and an iff characterization of failure by a typed missing-edge status. It instantiates concrete two-rule and three-rule encoded spaces on which search succeeds.
files.conclusion: Executable search over an explicit finite edge space is sound, complete when all successor edges are present, and otherwise reports a typed missing edge, with success on two- and three-rule witnesses.

files.summary: This file packages search over one explicit encoded edge space into soundness, completeness and typed missing-edge fields. It constructs the catalog from imported search theorems and projects search soundness and completeness. It transports cycle realization and additive and affine barriers from successful searches and exposes the independent closeout catalog.
files.conclusion: Every encoded search space yields soundness, completeness and missing-edge properties that transport cycle realization and barriers and project the independent closeout catalog.

files.summary: This file exposes the constructor-side hypothesis for arbitrary finite-cycle mutual recursion as a standalone builder with successor steps at each index. It transports the builder to the first-class finite-cycle schema and system with StepCtx and orientation predicates. It proves per-node cycle realization and additive and unbounded-affine contextual barriers for every builder realization.
files.conclusion: Every builder instance realizes its finite-cycle path and inherits additive and unbounded-affine contextual barriers.

files.summary: This file packages finite-cycle builders as search-certificate transports whose local successor edges are caller-supplied proof data. It defines transport to builders with StepCtx and affine witnesses. It proves certified per-node realization and additive and unbounded-affine barriers, and maps two-rule and three-rule constructor data and witness systems to certificates.
files.conclusion: Search certificates with caller-supplied successor proofs realize finite cycles and inherit additive and unbounded-affine barriers, with two- and three-rule instances.

files.summary: This file closes the theorem-visible H3 surface by packaging schema, builder, mapping, graph certificate, algorithmic search, typed missing-edge boundary and two-rule and three-rule instances into one finite closeout catalog. It defines ten canonical rows with theorem-covered versus typed-boundary statuses. It proves the canonical closeout catalog from the imported realization, barrier, soundness and completeness theorems.
files.conclusion: The ten-row H3 closeout catalog holds with theorem evidence for nine rows, typed-boundary evidence for the missing-edge row, and two- and three-rule instances.

files.summary: This file packages finite-cycle realization and additive and affine barrier fields for a supplied graph-search certificate. It constructs the full catalog from the certificate and projects search-certificate, builder, bridge, realization and barrier components. It states sufficiency of certified successor edges and proves cycle realization for two-rule and three-rule fixtures.
files.conclusion: Every graph-search certificate yields bridge equalities, cycle realization and additive and affine barriers, with two- and three-rule nonvacuity.

files.summary: This file inserts a theorem-visible layer between graph-edge search data and the finite-cycle certificate and builder surfaces. It derives local successor steps from certified edges and transports certificates to search certificates and builders. It inherits per-node realization and additive and unbounded-affine barriers and builds two-rule and three-rule graph certificates.
files.conclusion: Graph certificates with certified successor edges derive local steps and inherit cycle realization and additive and affine barriers, with two- and three-rule certificates.

files.summary: This file packages reusable two-rule and three-rule constructor data and re-expresses them as finite-cycle builders, mutual systems and K-cycle systems. It proves that any such instance realizes its finite-cycle path at each node. It re-expresses the existing concrete witness systems through those constructors and specializes additive and arbitrary-node affine barriers to them.
files.conclusion: Reusable two- and three-rule constructors realize finite-cycle paths and their concrete witnesses inherit additive and affine barriers.

files.summary: This file defines a bounded two-node alternating duplication schema and system with shared additive and affine profiles and a minimal root-plus-wrapper context. It constructs pump and two-step composite schemas and measure conversions with a wrapper-iteration lower bound. It proves that one full cycle defeats additive direct orienters and, under an unbounded pump, affine direct orienters and hence global contextual orientations.
files.conclusion: One alternating two-step duplicate defeats additive and, under unboundedness, affine orientations of the whole minimal-context relation.

files.summary: This file lifts delayed duplication from finite cyclic signatures to arbitrary graphs with shared constructors, indexed recursors, edge-local steps and explicit certified cycles. It builds concrete cycles from closed TransGen and round-trip witnesses with phase-wise realization. It proves additive, unbounded-affine, transparent-compositional and scalar-projection contextual barriers and their finite round-trip, SCC and existential wrappers.
files.conclusion: Any certified raw-graph delayed-duplication cycle blocks additive, unbounded-affine, transparent-compositional and scalar-projection global orientations, including via finite SCC witnesses.

files.summary: This file generalizes bounded two-node delayed duplication to a finite cyclic family of k+1 recursors where one cycle peels k+1 successors and nests k+1 wrappers. It defines additive and affine constructor-local measures and their transport to a one-cycle derived schema. It proves exact cycle realization and deduces that no additive and, under an unbounded pump, no affine measure orients the minimal context closure.
files.conclusion: No additive measure and, under an unbounded pump, no affine measure orients the minimal context closure of the finite cyclic delayed-duplication system.

files.summary: This file shows the finite k+1-node delayed-duplication development factors through the abstract one-cycle cycle-flow interface. It fixes a node, transports additive, affine and compositional measures, and builds an abstract cycle witness. It recovers additive, affine, transparent and several matrix no-go theorems as instances of the abstract metatheorems.
files.conclusion: All finite cyclic delayed-duplication barriers follow from the abstract cycle-flow metatheorems through the node-0 witness.

files.summary: This file lifts synchronized preserving SCCs from finite cyclic systems to an arbitrary directed graph with packet forwarding along edges. It builds explicit graph cycles from closed transitive-closure, round-trip, finite reachability, nontrivial SCC and existential witnesses. It proves that one certified cycle realizes synchronized exposure and blocks additive, affine, transparent and scalar-projection contextual orientations uniformly.
files.conclusion: Any certified graph cycle, whether from transitive closure, round-trip, finite reachability or a nontrivial SCC, blocks all considered contextual orientations.

files.summary: This module isolates the common proof pattern behind synchronized preserving SCC results into an abstract packet interface with latent packets, wrappers and a certified one-cycle path. It defines additive, affine and transparent measures plus wrapper dominance. It proves the target evaluation exceeds the source and derives the corresponding global orientation impossibilities including a scalar-projection lift.
files.conclusion: A realized synchronized payload cycle is incompatible with any decreasing additive, affine under dominance and unboundedness, transparent or projected orientation.

files.summary: This file defines a two-node SCC in which each root rule preserves an explicit payload count while a two-step cycle exposes two visible wrapper-carried copies on synchronized inputs. It proves preservation under root steps and context closure, realization of the synchronized cycle, and visible exposure. It derives unconditional additive and affine barriers, retaining the older wrapper-dominance statement as a corollary.
files.conclusion: No additive and, unconditionally, no affine measure orients the multiplicity-preserving two-node SCC cycle.

files.summary: This file shows the finite synchronized-packet preserving SCC development factors through the abstract payload-flow metatheorems. It equates wrapper iterations, builds a packet model and cycle witness at node zero, and transports additive, affine and packet-transparent measures. It recovers the additive, affine, transparent and matrix-functional global barriers from the smaller abstract interface.
files.conclusion: Finite preserving additive, affine, transparent and matrix-functional barriers all follow from the abstract payload-flow metatheorems.

files.summary: Defines finite cyclic preserving SCC syntax with explicit latent packets, a root expose rule, and minimal context closure. Proves payload multiplicity is preserved, visible payload grows over a cycle, and one full cycle is realized as a TransGen path. Proves additive measures increase from source to target so no additive measure orients the cycle globally. Proves a conditional affine no-go under wrapper dominance plus unboundedness and provides an affine escape orienting the cycle, packaging an exact maximality certificate.
files.conclusion: Additive orientation of the preserving finite cycle is impossible, and affine impossibility holds exactly under wrapper dominance with an escape when it fails.

files.summary: This module adds a packet-transparent extension for finite synchronized-packet preserving SCCs where latent packet constructors are evaluation-transparent bookkeeping. It proves packets collapse to the empty constant, wrapper nesting is strictly monotone, and the synchronized target exceeds the source. It derives compositional, global, scalar-projection and weighted matrix-functional impossibilities from visible wrapper exposure.
files.conclusion: No packet-transparent, scalar-projected or weighted matrix-functional measure orients the finite preserving synchronized cycle.

files.summary: This module defines delayed and packet-preserving presentations over an arbitrary relation R and assembles each into a raw graph or packet system. It introduces global-orientation and additive, affine, compositional and transparent measure abbreviations. Its theorems forward explicit round-trip, finite-reachability, nontrivial-SCC, computable-search, projection and unboundedness or dominance hypotheses to imported cycle and packet barriers, showing no global orientation holds.
files.conclusion: Every cyclic relation presentation admits no global orientation by the stated additive, affine, compositional-transparent or projected measure classes.

files.summary: This module packages the first-class two-rule mutual schema with its primary-schema projection and canonical source, midpoint and target composites. It defines uniform additive and affine measures with primary and two-step derived forms, plus a wrapper-pump lower bound. It defines the minimal context closure, global orientation, reusable realization data and the native one-cycle path with its extension seam into the delayed-cycle layer.
files.conclusion: The two-rule mutual schema carries a canonical one-cycle composite with a theorem-native context realization and path.

files.summary: This module lands additive and affine-unbounded barriers for the theorem-native mutual schema and its context relation. It transports the existing alternating two-node schemas, measures and systems into the first-class mutual layer and re-proves their barriers as instances. It supplies a concrete alternating-term witness system realizing the mutual one-cycle composite.
files.conclusion: The first-class mutual schema inherits additive and affine-unbounded barriers, and the older alternating development is an instance of it.

files.summary: This module lifts transparent-compositional and scalar-projection affine continuations from the abstract delayed-cycle layer to the finite-cycle mutual layer and then to the two-rule mutual schema. It defines the base projection schemas and transparent-compositional measures with primary-measure forgetful maps. It proves that transparency at the base or a strictly projecting unbounded affine witness blocks global orientation.
files.conclusion: Both the finite-cycle mutual layer and the two-rule mutual layer inherit transparent-compositional and scalar-projection affine barriers.

files.summary: This module defines transparent-compositional measures on the alternating SCC schema and their derived two-step form preserving transparency. It proves that uniform orientation of the bounded SCC composites contradicts transparency at the base. It lifts this to global context orientation and derives a matrix-functional barrier through a weighted scalar projection with an unbounded-range witness.
files.conclusion: Transparent-successor compositional measures and projected-unbounded matrix-functional measures cannot orient the alternating SCC context.

files.summary: This file exercises the finite SCC certificate, its round-trip theorem and the KO7 boundary coexistence bundle. It checks public names for certificates, round-trips and coexistence with DWO and context-root facts. It adds projections confirming the Bool two-node fully connected certificate and its mutual reachability.
files.conclusion: The Bool two-node certificate has distinct mutually reachable witnesses satisfying round-trip and coexistence.

files.summary: This file checks the mutual-duplication finite-schema API. It elaborates graph-search and final and closeout catalogs, cycle realization, additive and affine barriers and two- and three-rule witnesses. Five examples verify catalog inhabitation, transitive cycle reachability and additive and affine non-orientation.
files.conclusion: Cycles are realizable but additively and affinely unorientable in the two- and three-rule witnesses.

files.summary: The file checks the algorithmic-search final catalog and its API. It verifies search soundness, finite completeness, the missing-successor-edge boundary, cycle-realization transport and additive and affine barrier transport, and the closeout catalog. Five examples instantiate the catalog and executable search for the two-rule witness space and project them to closeout catalogs.
files.conclusion: The two-rule witness space yields an algorithmic-search final catalog whose executable search succeeds and projects to closeout catalogs.

files.summary: The file checks the encoded finite-cycle graph-search layer: edges, successor lookup, candidate assembly, searchCycle?, soundness and the none-iff-missing characterization. It also checks the two- and three-rule constructors and witness spaces. Two examples prove executable search succeeds for both witness spaces.
files.conclusion: Both two- and three-rule witness encoded spaces have executable searches that return cycle candidates.

files.summary: The file checks the builder-mapping search-certificate layer: certificates, builders, step and global-orient contexts, affine-at conditions, cycle realization and additive and affine barriers. It checks two- and three-rule constructors and witness certificates. One example proves transitive step closure from cycle source to target for the two-rule witness certificate.
files.conclusion: The two-rule witness search certificate realizes its cycle in transitive step closure.

files.summary: The file checks the finite-cycle builder layer: advance, builders and their K-cycle systems. It verifies cycle realization and additive and affine barrier theorems. Three existence examples reference the builder declarations, and two examples prove TransGen cycle realization for a general three-rule builder and for the two-rule witness builder.
files.conclusion: General three-rule builders and the two-rule witness builder realize cycles in transitive step closure.

files.summary: The file checks the closeout layer: H3 closeout rows, statuses, length, membership and nodup lemmas, projection to the finite schema, nonempty search space and the closeout catalog constructor. Three examples exhibit the closeout catalog, project its two-rule row to a final catalog, and project its second component to executable search success.
files.conclusion: The closeout catalog exists and its two-rule row supplies both a final catalog and a successful executable search.

files.summary: The file checks the mutual-duplication final catalog: the catalog constructor, projections to certificates, builders, cycle realization and additive and affine barriers, plus a certified-edge requirement and two nonvacuous witnesses. Seven examples project the two- and three-rule witness catalogs to nonempty certificates and builders, prove cycle realization in general and at base terms, and prove additive and affine unorientability.
files.conclusion: Final catalogs for the two- and three-rule witnesses are nonempty, realize cycles nonvacuously, and admit no globally orienting additive or unbounded-affine measures.

files.summary: The file checks graph-search certificates for finite-cycle mutual-duplication schemas. It covers certificate conversions and builders, two-rule and three-rule witness certificates, realization of a cycle source to target in the transitive closure of the step context, and round-trip of search-certificate builders. It also checks that additive measures and unbounded affine measures admit no global orienting context on those cyclic witnesses.
files.conclusion: The two- and three-rule cyclic witnesses realize their step cycles while admitting no global additive or unbounded-affine orienting context.

files.summary: The file checks finite-schema instances: two- and three-rule data, their mutual and K-cycle systems, cycle realization, witness equalities and witness barrier theorems. Eleven examples reference the constructors, prove cycle realization for general two- and three-rule data, prove witness-system equalities, and prove additive and affine unorientability for the witness systems.
files.conclusion: Two- and three-rule data realize cycles with matching witness systems that admit no globally orienting additive or unbounded-affine measures.

files.summary: The file checks the core finite schema and its instances: K-cycle no-additive and no-affine cycle theorems, cycle witnesses, global barriers, K-cycle affine conditions, projection from mutual systems, and realization via finite schema and K-nodes. Ten examples reference those declarations and prove transitive cycle realization for the two- and three-rule witness systems at base terms.
files.conclusion: Two- and three-rule witness systems realize cycles nonvacuously via the finite schema.

files.summary: The file checks schema-projection barriers: transparent-compositional and scalar-projection-affine unorientability for K-cycle and mutual systems, compositional-to-primary conversion, and projection schemas including projection at zero. Seven existence examples reference each of those declarations.
files.conclusion: Transparent-compositional and scalar-projection-affine measures cannot globally orient mutual-duplication cycles.

files.summary: The file checks mutual-schema barriers and realization: schema-level no-additive and no-affine cycle theorems, system-level global barriers, transfer to alternating-dup schemas, realization via mutual schema, and a two-step mutual-witness nonvacuous claim. Eight examples reference the barrier and transfer declarations and exhibit an intermediate-step witness for base terms.
files.conclusion: The mutual witness system connects cycle source to target in two steps and transfers additive and affine barriers to alternating-duplication schemas.
